what_it_does: LiDAR sensors measure distance by timing how long light takes to bounce off objects and return. Flash LiDAR uses single-photon avalanche diodes (SPADs)—sensors so sensitive they can detect individual photons—to achieve fast, high-resolution depth measurement. This paper solves a key challenge: when used outdoors under bright sunlight (120,000 lux of background light), the sensor becomes flooded with noise, washing out the signal from reflected laser pulses. The solution uses a chopped analog counter architecture that suppresses the constant background light while preserving the brief laser echo. The result: reliable 76-meter range measurements even in direct sunlight, enabling practical autonomous vehicle perception.
